speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To begin, could you please tell me how many weeks pregnant you are and when you last had a menstrual period? I also need to know how severe your abdominal pain is and if you have experienced any vaginal bleeding or fluid leakage.

speaker: Patient
text: 32-year-old woman, gravida 2, para 1, at 38 weeks' gestation. The patient reports experiencing vaginal bleeding for the past hour accompanied by severe abdominal pain. She mentions that she felt contractions before the onset of the bleeding, but the contractions ceased once the bleeding began. Her first childbirth was a cesarean section due to nonreassuring fetal heart rate.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you have any history of placenta previa or prior abdominal surgery, and have you noticed any vaginal fluid leakage? I need to assess your current vital signs and fetal heart rate immediately.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Vaginal bleeding. I also have Severe abdominal pain, History of contractions that stopped, Previous cesarean delivery.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your history of a previous cesarean section, the combination of severe abdominal pain and vaginal bleeding at 38 weeks is highly concerning for uterine rupture. I need to assess the fetal status and your stability immediately to determine if this is a surgical emergency. REQUEST TEST: Fetal_Heart_Rate_Monitoring, REQUEST TEST: Abdominal_Exam
